messages:
alex.chen: FYI customer reported stream dropping ~30s in. Request id rc-9f5b2a, attached a short log snippet showing a 502 then nothing. Can we get a minimal curl repro and check auth rotation?

maya.support: Thanks — can you paste the request_id and the exact time window? Also if they can share a curl they used that would help. :eyes:

support-bot: captured request rc-9f5b2a for org acme-inc, linked logs: /infra/logs/rc-9f5b2a (redacted). Auto tags: streaming, auth, proxy.

alex.chen: They say it starts streaming then suddenly a 401 or connection reset around 25-35s. Time window 2026-03-12T14:02:15Z — 14:03:00Z. No curl provided.

riley_sre: Can you try this quick curl to reproduce? Use HTTP/1.1 + no buffering to emulate SSE clients. Sample we ask customers to run: 

```bash
curl -N -v \n  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN>' \n  -H 'X-Request-Id: rc-9f5b2a' \n  -H 'Connection: keep-alive' \n  'https://api.redwood.run/v1/streams?model=gptx&stream=true'
```

Add `--http1.1` if curl defaults to http2 on their system. Also run with `--trace-ascii curl.trace` to capture headers.

maya.support: Also ask them to include the exact Authorization header (mask token), proxy (if any), and whether they have signed cookies. Proxy middleboxes often buffer and drop SSE.

alex.chen: Ran the above against customer's reported token (masked). Repro: stream starts, then at ~28s we get: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` and then connection close. Trace shows `Proxy-Authenticate: Negotiate` from upstream.

riley_sre: That suggests token rotation or proxy reauth. Two quick checks: 1) rerun but refresh a new token immediately before curl start; 2) run `curl --no-buffer --http1.1 -v --trace-ascii trace.txt` to capture full handshake and chunk boundaries. Also include `-H 'X-Forwarded-For: <client-ip>'` if they use a proxy.

maya.support: Can you upload the curl.trace and we can pull the debug bundle? If it's a customer-managed proxy we need to ask them to check keep-alive timeouts.

logs-bot: debug bundle created: bundles/rc-9f5b2a/stream-handshake-2141592653.tar.gz (expires in 7d). Contains runtime logs, ingress nginx traces, and auth service tokens (redacted).

alex.chen: Uploaded trace.txt and curl.trace to the bundle. Observed `Proxy: 1.1` header and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. The curl trace shows a 401 response with WWW-Authenticate header coming from the corporate proxy at t+27s.

riley_sre: Good find. Two possible root causes: token TTL shorter than session (rotated mid-stream) or proxy performing NTLM/Negotiate reauth on long-lived connections. For repro we should try a token that has long TTL and bypass the proxy (direct network) to confirm.

maya.support: I'll message the customer with a short checklist to run the two repros: (1) rerun with fresh long-lived token and `--http1.1 --no-buffer`, upload trace; (2) rerun while bypassing corporate proxy or set `--proxy ''` and upload trace. Provide them the exact curl block above.

alex.chen: Customer ran both. Bypass proxy -> stream stable past 5 minutes. With proxy -> 401 at ~28s. So proxy is the cause. Customer's IT team confirmed an authentication handshake TTL of 30s for the proxy.

riley_sre: OK root cause confirmed: proxy auth timeout. Proposed mitigations: a) recommend using token that can be refreshed transparently or use connection keepalive with proxy that supports NTLM keep-alive; b) implement graceful reconnect in client with Authorization refresh mid-stream (server-side we already support resume for some models, but client reconnect/follow-on request required); c) add a KB article for customers behind NTLM/Negotiate proxies.

maya.support: I'll draft KB and reply to customer with recommended curl/test steps + network config notes. Opening ticket INF-4823 to track KB + SDK client reconnect patterns. Assigning to riley_sre. :memo:

riley_sre: Got it — will also add an internal note to add a diagnostic to our SSE handshake logs to surface proxy `WWW-Authenticate` headers earlier.

alex.chen: Closing loop with customer. Thanks team :tada:
